का.आ. 3476(अ).--रेलवे अधिनियम, 1989 (1989 का 24) की धारा 20ए की उप-धारा () द्वारा प्रदत्त 
शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए (इसके पश्चात उक्त अधिनियम के रूप में संदर्भित), केंद्र सरकार इस बात से संतुष्ट होने के 
पश्चात कि सार्वजनिक प्रयोजन के लिए भूमि, जिसका संक्षिप्त विवरण संलग्न अनुसूची में दिया गया है, विशेष रेलवे 
परियोजना अर्थात आंध्र प्रदेश राज्य के तिरुपति जिले में “येपेंड-पुडि स्टेशनों के बीच बाईपास लाइन (25.36 किमी.)” के 
निष्पादन के लिए आवश्यक है, Ug ऐसी भूमि का अधिग्रहण करने की अपनी मंशा की घोषणा करती है; 


उक्त भूमि में हितबद्ध कोई भी व्यक्ति, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 20डी की उप-धारा (1) के अंतर्गत पूर्वोक्त प्रयोजन 
के लिए ऐसी भूमि के अधिग्रहण और उपयोग के संबंध में आधिकारिक राजपत्र में इस अधिसूचना के प्रकाशन की तारीख से 
तीस दिनों की अवधि के भीतर भू-अर्जन में अपनी आपत्ति दर्ज करा सकता है. 


प्रत्येक ऐसी आपत्ति, सक्षम प्राधिकारी, अर्थात राजस्व मंडल अधिकारी (भूमि अधिग्रहण), श्रीकालहस्ती, तिरुपति 
जिले को लिखित रूप में की जाएगी और उसके आधारों को निर्धारित की जाएगी तथा सक्षम प्राधिकारी अर्थात राजस्व 
मंडल अधिकारी (भूमि अधिग्रहण), श्रीकालहस्ती, तिरुपति जिला आपकत्तिकर्ता को व्यक्तिगत रूप से या कानूनी व्यवसायी 
द्वारा सुनवाई का अवसर देगा और ऐसी सभी आपत्तियों को सुनने के बाद तथा आगे ऐसी की जांच करने के पश्चात यदि 
सक्षम प्राधिकारी यह आवश्यक समझता है तो वह किसी आदेश द्वारा आपत्तियों को स्वीकार या अस्वीकार कर सकता है.

इस अधिसूचना के अंतर्गत शामिल की गई भूमि की भू-योजनाएं और अन्य विवरण उक्त सक्षम प्राधिकारी के 
कार्यालय में उपलब्ध हैं और इच्छुक व्यक्ति द्वारा उनका निरीक्षण किया जा सकता है.

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(South Central Railway) 
NOTIFICATION 
Secunderabad , the 21st July, 2025 

S.O. 3476(E).—In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (I) of section 20A of the Railway Act, 
1989 (24 of 1989) (hereinafter referred as in as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for the 
public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule annexed hereto, is required for the 
purpose of execution of the Special Railway Project namely, “Bypass line between Yerpedu—Pudi stations (25.36 
Km.)”, in Tirupati district in the state of Andhra Pradesh, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land: 

Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of thirty days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the official gazette, raise objections to the acquisition and use of such land for the aforesaid purpose 
under sub- section (1) of section 20D of the said act: 

Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely Revenue Divisional Officer (land 
acquisition), Srikalahasthi, Tirupati district in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent 
Authority namely Revenue Divisional Officer (land acquisition), Srikalahasthi, Tirupati district shall give the objector 
an opportunity of being heard, either in person or by legal practitioner and may, after hearing all such objections and 
after making such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or 
disallow the objections. 

Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (I) of section 20(D) of the said act shall be 
final. 

The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL SERVICES CENTRES AUTHORITY 
NOTIFICATION 
Gandhinagar, the 24th July, 2025 


INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL SERVICES CENTRES AUTHORITY (FUND MANAGEMENT) (AMENDMENT) 
REGULATIONS, 2025 


IFSCA/GN/2025/007.—In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (l) of Section 28 read with 
sub-section (l) of Section 2 and sub-section (l) of Section 3 of the International Financial Services Centres 
Authority Act, 209, and Section 28C of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 992, the International 
Financial Services Centres Authority hereby makes the following regulations, further to amend the International 
Financial Services Centres Authority (Fund Management) Regulations, 2025, (hereinafter referred to as the 
principal regulations), namely: - 


l. () These regulations may be called the International Financial Services Centres Authority (Fund Management) 
(Amendment) Regulations, 2025. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. In Chapter VI titled “OTHER FUND MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES’, after regulation 07 of the principal 
regulations, the following Part shall be inserted, namely: — 
PART D: THIRD-PARTY FUND MANAGEMENT SERVICES 
07A. A FME may launch a scheme on behalf of a third-party in accordance with the provisions of this Part. 
Definitions 
07B. For the purpose of this Part: 


i. “third-party fund management services” or “third-party fund management arrangement” refers to the 
activity wherein a Registered FME manages the schemes on behalf of a third-party; 


ii. “third-party fund manager” means and includes an entity registered or regulated, for the purposes of 
fund management, portfolio management, investment advisory or any other similar activity, by 
whatever name called, with the concerned financial sector regulator in the country of its incorporation, 
and which avails the third-party fund management services from a Registered FME 


Obligation to seek Authorisation and compliances 


07C. (l) A FME intending to set up and manage schemes on behalf of a third-party shall seek authorisation from 
the Authority under this Part for undertaking third-party fund management services in accordance with the 
terms and conditions specified in this Part and shall comply with other conditions as may be specified by 


6 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


the Authority from time to time. 


Explanation. — Such FME may also set up schemes, offer Portfolio Management Services or carry out other 
activities as permitted under these regulations, as per the category of its registration, wherein a third-party 
fund management arrangement is not involved. 


(2) The FME shall be responsible for strengthening its overall compliance function and shall deploy 
resources commensurate to the size of its operations in the IFSC, so as to ensure adequate focus on the 
compliance for each scheme. 


(3) The FME and the fiduciaries shall ensure compliance with this Part. 


(4) Notwithstanding any arrangement of FME with the third-party including the indemnification 
arrangement, the FME shall continue to be liable for any and all obligations or liabilities arising in 
connection with the third-party fund management arrangement. 


Legal Form of the FME 


07D. (i) The FME seeking authorisation under this Part shall be set up in the IFSC in the form of a company, 
limited liability partnership (LLP) or any other form as may be permitted by the Authority. 


(2) In case of a company, its memorandum of association, and in case of a LLP, its limited liability 
partnership agreement, shall contain a provision enabling it to offer third-party fund management services. 


Appointment of Principal Officers and other Key managerial personnel 


l07E. (() For each scheme managed under the third-party fund management arrangement, the FME shall appoint 
a dedicated person as the Principal Officer who shall be responsible for the overall activities with respect to 
that scheme, including but not limited to fund management, risk management and compliance. 


(2) In case of a Registered FME (Non-Retail), the Compliance Officer for its self-managed schemes or 
Portfolio Management Services may also act as the Compliance Officer for the schemes managed under the 
third-party fund management arrangement. 


(3) In case of a Registered FME (Retail), the Compliance Officer for its Retail Schemes shall be separate 
from the Compliance Officer for the Non-Retail Schemes that are either self-managed or managed through 
third-party fund management arrangement. 


(4) For appointment of additional KMP in terms of sub-regulation (4) of regulation 7, the AUM of the 
schemes managed under the third-party fund management arrangement shall also be considered, excluding 
the AUM of fund of funds schemes managed under third-party fund management arrangement. 


(5) Any appointment or changes in the KMPs appointed under sub-regulations () and (3) of this regulation 
shall be carried out in the manner specified by the Authority. 


Net worth requirement 


l07F. A FME seeking authorisation to offer third-party fund management services shall, at all times, maintain an 
additional net worth of USD 500,000 or such other amount as may be specified by the Authority; 


Explanation. — Such net worth shall be separate and in addition to: 


(i) the minimum net worth requirements applicable for its activities as a FME for the schemes, 
Portfolio Management Services or any other activities as permitted under these regulations as per 
the category of its registration, wherein a third-party fund management arrangement is not 
involved; and 


(ii) the minimum net worth requirements applicable for any other activities within or outside the 
IFSC. 
Schemes under third-party fund management arrangement 


07G. (l) A FME shall manage Restricted Schemes under third-party fund management arrangement in 
accordance with and in the manner as specified under Part B of Chapter III of these regulations: 


Provided that such scheme does not exceed the corpus of USD 50 million or such other value as may be 
specified by the Authority. 


(2) The third-party, under the third-party fund management arrangement, shall be deemed to be an 
associate of the FME for the purpose of compliance with the requirements specified under sub-regulation 3 
of regulation 35, sub-regulation 4 of regulation 35 and regulation 40. 


[भागवता---खण्ड 4] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


Eligibility of ‘third-party’ 


07H. A FME may provide third-party fund management services only to such third-party who is a third-party 
fund manager and meets the following criteria, namely: 


(a) It is incorporated either in India, IFSC or a foreign jurisdiction; 
(b) It allocates adequate resources to discharge its functions; 
(c) The persons responsible for its functions have adequate and requisite experience; and, 


(d) The third-party, its officers, directors/ partners/ designated partners, key managerial personnel and 
controlling shareholders are ‘fit and proper’ persons in terms of regulation 9. 


Explanation.- A third-party fund manager shall be eligible to avail third-party fund management services 
even if its ultimate or interim parent entity is not engaged in the fund management activities. 


Disclosures to investors 


l07I. For the Restricted Schemes that are managed under the third-party fund management services, besides 
making disclosures under regulation 36, the FME shall make the following disclosures under a separate 
head / section at a prominent place in the placement memorandum: 


(a) Details of the third-party and the persons who effectively conduct the business of such third-party; 
(b) Details of the segregated responsibilities of the FME and such third-party; 


(c) Potential conflicts of interest that may arise due to the third-party fund management arrangement 
along with the measures proposed to avoid, resolve and mitigate such conflicts; and 


(d) such other disclosures as may be specified by the Authority. 
Risk Management 
07J. |The FMEs shall have the following risk management measures in place: 


(a) An internal policy comprising of a comprehensive risk management framework to identify and 
address the unique risks associated with third-party fund management and conflicts emerging from 
the same; 


(b) Segregation of funds and operational independence for all the schemes, whether under self- 
management or third-party fund management; 


(c) Existing mechanism to address the investors’ complaints and disputes is extended to the complaints 
and disputes of the investors of the schemes under third-party fund management arrangement; 


(d) An internal policy for conducting periodic internal audits and reviews to ensure compliances with 
the regulatory requirements with respect to third-party fund management; and the submission of the 
report thereon to the fiduciaries; and 


(e) Such other measures as may be specified by the Authority. 
Other obligations of the FME 
07K. (l) It shall be the duty of the FME to ensure that- 
(a) the third-party meets the eligibility criteria as specified under regulation 07H; 


(b) the schemes set up by the FME under the third-party fund management arrangement are treated to 
be the schemes of the FME; 


(c) the liability of the FME towards any Restricted Scheme and its investors is not affected due to the 
third-party fund management services; 


(d) the third-party is qualified and capable of undertaking the entrusted functions, and that such third- 
party was onboarded with due care and caution; 


(e) the activities undertaken by the third-party are monitored by the FME and in doing so, the FME may 
issue such instructions to such third-party as it may deem necessary; 


(f) the third-party fund management arrangement enables the FME to terminate the arrangement at any 
time, in the interest of investors or on the directions of the Authority; 


(g) it reviews the services rendered by each third-party on an ongoing basis and periodically shares 
these reports with the respective fiduciaries; 


8 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART III—SEc.4] 


(h) a suitable indemnity mechanism is in place which requires the third-party to indemnify the FME 
from any potential liabilities arising from the funds managed under the third-party fund 
management arrangement; 


(i) it pays such fees within such timelines as specified by the Authority, and 
(j) such other requirements as may be specified by the Authority. 


(2) The FME shall be responsible for all the acts of omissions and commission of the third-party in relation 
to the third-party fund management services; 


Miscellaneous 


l07L. All other relevant provisions of these regulations including the circulars or guidelines, if any, issued 
thereunder, unless specified otherwise, shall mutatis mutandis apply to the FMEs authorised under this Part 
for the schemes managed under the third-party fund management arrangement. 


l07M. This part shall not be applicable to such schemes of FME wherein the parent entity or any associate of the 
FME provides any fund management related support or advice to the FME.”

making such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority for Land Acquisition (CALA) thinks necessary, by 
order, either allow or disallow the objections;

said Act shall be final; The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and 
can be inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority (CALA).

फा. सं. एम/471/2025-एएसडी.---जहां एक ओर आधार संख्या का उपयोग पहचान स्थापित करने के लिए व्यक्तियों को 
सब्सिडी, लाभ और सेवाएं सुविधाजनक और सहज ढंग से प्राप्त करने में सक्षम बनाता है, जिससे पहचान स्थापित करने के लिए अनेक 
दस्तावेजों की आवश्यकता समाप्त होती है, प्रक्रियाएं सरल होती हैं तथा पारदर्शिता और दक्षता को बढ़ावा मिलता है: 


जहां एक ओर भारत सरकार के इलेक्ट्रॉनिकी और सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी मंत्रालय, भारतीय विशिष्ट पहचान प्राधिकरण 
(यूआईडीएआई) से परामर्श के उपरांत, अपने दिनांक 15, मई 2025 के पत्र संख्या ई एफ संख्या: 13(2)/2020-ईजी-1॥।(वॉल्यूम-8), 
के माध्यम से राष्ट्रीय सूचना-विज्ञान केंद्र, इलेक्ट्रॉनिकी और सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी मंत्रालय (जिसे आगे “उक्त मंत्रालय”,”उक्त विभाग” 
अथवा “उक्त एजेंसी” के रूप में संदर्भित किया गया है), भारत सरकार(जिसे आगे “उक्त सरकार” कहा गया है) को सुशासन के लिए 
आधार प्रमाणीकरण (सामाजिक कल्याण, नवाचार, ज्ञान) नियम, 2020 (जिसे आगे “उक्त नियम” के रूप में संदर्भित किया गया है) के

F. No. M/471/2025-ASD —Whereas the use of Aadhaar number to establish identity enables individuals to receive 
subsidies, benefits and services in a convenient and seamless manner, obviates the need for multiplicity of documents to 
establish identity, simplifies processes and promotes transparency and efficiency: 


And whereas the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India, after consultation with 
the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAD), had allowed vide its letter no. eF.No: 13(2)/2020-EG-II(Vol-8), dated 
15May, 2025 to the National Informatics Centre, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Ministry or the said department or the said Agency), Government of INDIA (hereinafter referred to as 
the said Government) for the purposes prescribed under sub-rule (1) of rule 3 of the Aadhaar Authentication for Good 
Governance (Social Welfare, Innovation, Knowledge) Rules, 2020 (hereinafter referred to as the said rules) that the said 
Government/Ministry/Department/Agency may be allowed to perform authentication and be permitted the use of Aadhaar 
number during authentication for establishing identity of Aadhaar number holder whose purpose for use of Aadhaar 
authentication has been allowed under section 4(4)(b)(i) or 4(4)(b)(ii) or 7 of Aadhaar Act. 


And whereas, the Aadhaar authentication shall be performed for authentication of beneficiaries/users of delivery 
(benefits/services) under schemes/initiatives of Central and State Governments (hereinafter referred to as the said purpose) 
as prescribed under sub-rule (1) of rule 3 of the said rules and the performance of Aadhaar authentication for the said 
purpose shall be on voluntary basis and that the said Ministry/Department/Agency shall perform the Aadhaar authentication 
only for identification of beneficiaries/users of delivery (benefits/services) under schemes/initiatives of Central and State 
Governments through Beneficiary Satyapan Application (BSA) [hereinafter referred to as the use case(s)]. 


Now, therefore, in pursuance of rule 5 of the said rules read with sub-clause (i) or (1) of clause (b) of sub-section 
(4) of section 4 or section 7 of the Act, NIC hereby notifies the following, namely: — 


1. Authentication of beneficiaries for establishing the identity of Aadhaar number holder may be carried out by the 
concerned Ministry/Department/Agency only for the purposes wherein use of Aadhaar authentication has been 
allowed under section 4(4)(b)(i) or 4(4)(b)(ii) or 7 of Aadhaar Act.

number holder for the purpose of authentication herein.

Ministry/Department/Agency shall inform to the Aadhaar number holder of alternate and viable means of 
identification and shall not deny any service to the Aadhaar number holder for refusing to, or being unable to,

G.S.R. 515(E).—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Department of Parliamentary Affairs (Recruitment and Condition of Service) Rules, 1963, in so far 
as they relate to the post of Stenographer, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such 
supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of 
Stenographer Grade ‘D’ (Group-‘C’ post) in the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, namely: - 


1. Short title and commencement.—(1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, 
Stenographer Grade ‘D’ (Group-‘C’ post) Recruitment Rules, 2025. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2 Number of post, classification and level in the pay matrix. —The number of the said post, its 
classification and the level in the pay matrix attached thereto, shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the 
Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3: Method of recruitment, age-limit and qualifications, etec—The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said 
Schedule. 


4. Disqualifications. — No person, — 
(a) who has entered into or contracted marrieage with a person having a spouse living: or 
(b) who having a spouse living has entered into or contracted a marrieage with any person. 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for doing so, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


3: Power to relax.—Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient to do so, 
it may, by order, for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any 
class or category of persons. 


6. Saving.—Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, ex-Servicemen 
and other special categories of persons, in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to 
time in this regard.

S.O. 3544(E).— Whereas, it appears to the Central Government that it is necessary in the public

the date on which the copies of this notification, as published in the Gazette of India, are made available to 
the General Public, object in writing to the acquisition of the right of user therein or laying of the pipeline 
under the land to Shri Rajiv Kumar Pandey(Retd. ADM), Indian Oil Corporation Limited, New Mundra 
Panipat Pipeline Project, FCI Aravali Gypsum & Minerals India Limited (FAGMIL) Building, 1* Floor

NOTIFICATION 
Jaipur, the 29th July, 2025 


S.O. 3545(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 20A of the Railway 
(Amendment) Act, 2008 (11 of 2008) and the Railway Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) hereinafter referred to as the said Act. 
The central Government, after being satisfied that for the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which has 
been given in the schedule annexed hereto, is required for execution, maintenance, management and operation of 
Special Railway Project of namely: "Luni-Samdari-Bhildi Doubling Railway Project (Special Rail Project) of the 
District Jalore in the state of Rajasthan hereby declares its intention to acquire such land; 


Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of thirty days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for the aforesaid purpose 
under sub-section (1) of section 20D of the said Act; 


Every such objection shall be made to the competent authority, namely, Sub Divisional officer, Raniwara, 
District Jalore, Rajasthan in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof, and the competent authority, shall give the 
objector an opportunity of being heard, either in person or by legal practitioner and may, after hearing all such 
objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, as the competent authority thinks necessary, by order, either 
allow or disallow the objections; 


Any order made by the competent authority under sub-section (2) if section 20D of the said Act shall be 
final; 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the competent authority.

परिवहन और राजमार्ग मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना संख्या का.आ. 3219(अ) तारीख 08/08/2024, जो भारत के राजपत्र, 
असाधारण, भाग Il, खण्ड 3, उपखंड (1) में प्रकाशित की गई थी, द्वारा गुजरात राज्य के कच्छ जिले में NH 754K के 
कि.मी. 54.400 से कि.मी. 141.00 तक के भू-खण्ड के निर्माण (चौड़ीकरण/पेव्ड शोल्डर सहित 2-लेन/4-लेन का बनाना 
आदि), अनुरक्षण, प्रबंधन और प्रचालन के लिए उस अधिसूचना से उपाबद्ध अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का अर्जन करने के 
अपने आशय की घोषणा की थी ; 


और उक्त अधिसूचना का सार उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3क की उपधारा (3) के अधीन तारीख "25/08/2024 "

जबकि सक्षम प्राधिकारी को धारा 3-ग के तहत दायर आपत्ति प्राप्त हुई है, जिस पर विचार किया गया है और 
उसका उचित रूप से निपटान किया गया; 


और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ की उपधारा (1) के अनुसरण में, केन्द्रीय सरकार को अपनी 
रिपोर्ट दे दी है ; 


अतः अब, केन्द्रीय सरकार, सक्षम प्राधिकारी की उक्त रिपोर्ट प्राप्त हो जाने पर और उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ 
की उपधारा (1) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, यह घोषणा करती है कि उक्त अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का 
पूर्वोक्त प्रयोजन के लिए अर्जन किया जाना चाहिए ;

5.0. 3539(E).—Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India, in the Ministry of Railway (North 
Central Railway, Construction department), Notification number, S.O. 96 (E) dated the 6th April, 2025 published 
in Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part-II, Section 3 Sub Section (ii), dated 7th June, 2025 (hereinafter referred to 
as the said notification) and issue under sub-section (l) of section 20A of the Railways (Amendment) Act. 2008 (llof 
2008) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declares its intention to acquire the land 
specified in the schedule annexed the said notification for the purpose of Design, Supply, Erection, Testing & 
Commissioning of Sub-Sectioning & Paralleling Post (SSP) of Special Railway Project, namely Special Railway 
Project of Raising of Speed to 60kmph/200kmph on existing New Delhi-Hawrah route (incl. Kanpur- 
Lucknow) in District Hathras of the state of Uttar Pradesh. 


And, whereas, the substance of the said notification was published in the daily newspapers "Dainik Jagran" 
and "The Times of India" Dated 22 June, 2025 under sub-section (4) of section 20A of the said Act; 


And whereas, all the objections received in this project have been disposed of by the Competent Authority; 


And, whereas, in pursuance of sub-section 20E of the said Act, the Competent Authority has submitted its 
report the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the report of the Competent Authority, and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by sub-section (l) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the lands 
specified in the schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And, further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the official Gazette, the land specified in the Schedule annexed here 
to shall vest absolutely in the Central Government free from all encumbrances. 


And, that all persons interested in the above mentioned land in pursuance of sub-section (04) of section 20(F) 
of the said Act by the Central Government are hereby informed that they may, personally or through an agent or legal 
practitioner, be notified by the competent authority Sub Divisional Magistrate, Sasni/SLAO Hathras, can submit 
his claim in the next 20 days from the date of publication of this notification in the office of the Competent Authority.

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 31st July, 2025 

5.0. 3542(E).—Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways, S.0.3105 (E).Dated: 02.08.2024, published in Gazette of India,Extraordinary, Part II, 
Section 3, Sub-section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) 
(here in after referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in 
the Schedule annexed to the said notification for construction,maintenance, management and operation of 
NH266.( Karad to Tasgaon) in the stretch of landfrom Km. 25.550 to Km. 43.300 (Tupari to Bambavde) in the 
district of Sangli in the state of Maharashtra. 


And whereas the substance of the said notification S.O.3105 (E).Dated: 02.08.2024 has been published in 
"The Dainik Sakal" dated 24 August 2024 & “Times of India” Dated 15 August 2024 under sub-section (3) of 
section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas objections filed under section 3-C, considered and settled the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act,the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


24 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(11)] 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section Additional 3D of the said Act, the Central 
Government hereby declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the 
said Schedule shall vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(Central Railway) 
NOTIFICATION 
Mumbai, the 31st July, 2025 
Under clause 20E of the Railway (Amendment) Act 2008 


S.O. 3552(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Railways 
(Railway Board), number, 5.0. 4381 (E) dated 197 September 2022 published in Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part 
II, section 3 Sub-section (ii), dated the 20 September 2022 (hereinafter referred to as the said notification ) and issued 
under sub-section (1) of section 20A of the Railway Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) and Railway (Amendment) Act, 2008 
(11 of 2008) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declares its intention to acquire the land 
specified in the schedule annexed to the said notification for the purpose of execution, maintenance, management and 
operation of Special Railway Project, namely Pachora-Jamner with Extension upto Malkapur-Narrow Gauge to 
Broad Gauge (84.34 Km) in the district of Jalgaon in the State of Maharashtra. 


And whereas, the substance of the said notification was published in for SLAO(1) UTPH.Jalgaon daily 
Marathi newspapers namely “Dainik Deshonnati” & “Punyanagari” Dated 18-07-2024 under sub section (4) of 
section 20A of the said Act; 


And whereas, objections were received. Competent Authority has heard the objections and orders have been 
passed in terms of Section D of the said act; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of Section 20E of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now therefore, upon receipt of the report of the Competent Authority and in exercise of the powers conferred 
by sub-section (1) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the lands specified in the 
schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose;And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of 
section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that on publication of this notification in the official 
Gazette, the land specified in the schedule annexed hereto shall vest absolutely in the Central government free from all 
encumbrances.

आईपीडीएमएस के माध्यम से जारी करें तथा उसकी एक प्रति राज्य औषधि नियंत्रकों और विनिर्माता वितरकों को जारी करें। 


(a) औषधि (मूल्य नियंत्रण) आदेश, 2043 के 24 (4) के अनुसार प्रत्येक फुटकर विक्रेता और वितरक विनिर्माता द्वारा दिए गए 


रूप में ऐसे परिसर, जहां कारबार को इस प्रकार किया जा रहा है कि उससे परामर्श के इच्छुक किसी व्यक्ति के लिए पहुंच 
आसान हो, वहां उसके किसी सुस्पष्ट भाग पर कीमत सूची और पूरक सूची, यदि कोई हो, को प्रदर्शित करेगा। 


(=) उल्लिखित खुदरा मूल्य केवल उपर्युक्त निर्माता/विपणन के लिए लागू है जैसा कि उन्होंने औषधि (मूल्य नियंत्रण) आदेश, 


2043 के तहत अनुबद्ध मूल्य निर्धारण/संशोधन के लिए फॉर्म | पर जमा किया गया था और सरकार द्वारा निर्धारित सभी 
लागू वैधानिक आवश्यकताओं की पूर्ति के अधीन प्रासंगिक विधियों/नियमों के अन्तर्गत जैसा कि केन्द्रीय/राज्य लाइसेंसिंग 
ऑथोरिटी के सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा मैन्यूफैक्चरिंग लाइसेंस मंजूरी के तहत संबंधित विनिर्मित निर्माता/विपणन कम्पनियां 
जो अनुपालन करती हैं। 


(च) विनिर्माता या विपणन कम्पनी, उपरोक्त विनिर्मितियों और विनिर्दिष्ट शर्तों का पालन नहीं करती है तो वे आवश्यक वस्तुएँ 


अधिनियम, 7955 के साथ पठित डीपीसीओ, 203 के प्रावधानों के अधीन ब्याज सहित अधिप्रभारित राशि को जमा करने 
के लिए उत्तरदायी होंगे। 


(छ) इस आदेश में उपरोक्त तालिका के कॉलम (3) और (5) में तत्स्थानी प्रविष्टियों में निर्दिष्ट विनिर्माण और विपणन कंपनियों की 


प्रबलता और नाम के साथ, उपरोक्त तालिका के कॉलम (2) में निर्दिष्ट ऐसे फॉर्मूलेशन के खुदरा मूल्य के निर्धारण के 
परिणामस्वरूप, कॉलम (2), (3) और (5) में तत्स्थानी प्रविष्टियों में यथा निर्दिष्ट उस विनिर्माण और विपणन कंपनियों के 
लिए निर्दिष्ट स्ट्रेंथय के साथ फॉर्मूलेशन के खुदरा मूल्य को निर्धारित करने वाले कोई मूल्य आदेश यदि इस अधिसूचना से पहले 
जारी किए गए हो, तो उसे इसका स्थान लिया माना जाएगा।

G.S.R. 522(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Central Civil Accounts Service (Accountant and Senior Accountant Group ‘C’ posts) Recruitment 
Rules, 200, in so far as they relate to the post of Senior Accountant, except as respects things done or omitted to be 
done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to 
the post of Senior Accountant of the Central Civil Accounts Service, namely:- 


l. Short title and commencement. - (|) These rules may be called the Central Civil Accounts Service (Senior 
Accountant Group ‘B’ Non-Gazetted post) Recruitment Rules, 2025. 

(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Application. - These rules shall apply to the posts specified in column () of the Schedule annexed to these 


rules.

4. Method of recruitment, age limit, educational qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age limit, 
educational qualifications and other matters relating thereto shall be as specified in columns (5) to (3) of the Schedule 
annexed to these rules. 


5. Disqualification. - No person,- 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 


shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage, and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from operation of this rule. 


6. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order, for reasons to be recorded in writing, in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission, relax 
any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


7. Savings. - Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age limit and other concessions required 
to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, other backward classes, the Ex- Servicemen and other 
special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this 
regard.

Navjyoti” and “Rajasthan Patrika” Dated 17 May-2025 & 15 June-2025 under sub section (4) of section 20A of the

accordingly orders have been passed.

specified in the schedule annexed here to shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose;

the 25" February, 2025, in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (i), dated the 257 February, 
2025, inviting objections and suggestions from all persons likely to be affected thereby before the expiry of the period 
of thirty days from the date on which copies of Gazette containing the said notification were made available to the public;

considered by the Central Government.

G.S.R. 520(E).—In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section(I) of section 20A of the Railways Act,

execution of the Special Railway Project, namely Samakhiyali Gandhidham Quadrupling Project (53.00 KM) in 
District Kutch in the State of Gujarat, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land: 


Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of thirty days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for a foresaid purpose under 
sub-section (l) of section 20D of the said Act: 


Every such objection shall be made to the competent authority, namely, Prant Officer- Bhachau, District 
Kutch, in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the competent authority shall give the objector an 
opportunity of being heard, either in person or by legal practitioner and may, after hearing all such objections and after 
making such further enquiry, if any as the competent authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the 
objections. Any order made by the competent authority under sub-section (II) of section 20(D) of the said act shall be 
final. 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the competent authority.

New Delhi, the 3ist July, 2025 


G.S.R. 524(E).—In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (l) read with clauses (a) and (c) of 
sub-section (2) of section 55 of the Sashastra Seema Bal Act, 2007 (53 of 2007), the Central Government hereby 
makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the posts of Assistant Sub-Inspector(Electrician), 
Head Constable (Carpenter), Head Constable (Washerman), Head Constable (Barber), Head Constable (Gardener), 
Head Constable (Cobbler), Head Constable (Safaiwala), Head Constable (Cook), Head Constable (Waiter), Head 
Constable (Water Carrier) and Head Constable (Tailor), Engineering and Tradesmen Cadre under the Ministry of 
Home Affairs, namely:- 


l. Short title and commencement.- (|) These rules may be called the Ministry of Home Affairs, Sashastra Seema 
Bal, Combatised, Engineering and Tradesmen Cadre (Group ‘C’ Posts) Recruitment Rules, 2025. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Application .- These rules shall apply to the posts as specified in column (l) of the Schedule annexed to these 
rules. 


3. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix .- The number of the said posts, their classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedule. 


4. Method of recruitment, age limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said posts shall be as specified in columns (5) to (I3) of the said Schedule. 


5. Disqualification .- No person,— 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said posts: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such a marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to the person and other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt any 
person from the operation of this rule.

6. Initial constitution.- The incumbents holding the posts as specified in the Schedule, who were appointed to 
the posts as before the commencement of these rules on regular basis shall be deemed to have been appointed under 
the provisions of these rules in the respective grades immediately before the commencement of these rules, shall be 
taken into account for the purposes of probation period, qualifying service for promotion, confirmation and pension in 
the service. 


7. Medical fitness. Notwithstanding anything contained in these rules, only those persons who are in the 
medical category of SHAPE-I, as specified in the Ministry of Home Affairs guidelines for recruitment medical 
examinations in the Central Armed Police Forces and Assam Rifles, shall be eligible for appointment under the 
provisions of these rules. 


8. Superannuation. — Every person appointed under these rules shall retire from service on the afternoon of the 
last day of the month in which he or she attains the age of sixty years: 


Provided that the person whose date of birth is on the first day of the month, shall retire from service in the 
afternoon of the last day of the preceding month on attaining the age of superannuation. 


9. Liability of service.- Any person, appointed to the said posts under these rules shall be liable to serve 
anywhere in India or abroad. 


0. Interpretation.- If any question relating to the interpretation of these rules arises, it shall be decided by the 
Central Government. 


i. Power to relax .— Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, 
it may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any 
class or category of persons. 


2. Saving — Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex- 
servicemen and other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government 
from time to time in this regard

NOTIFICATION 
Jaipur, the Ist August, 2025 


S.O. 3560(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India, in the Ministry of Railways (North 
Western Railway, Construction organization), Notification number, 5.0. 820 (E) dated 2274 April, 2025 published in 
Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, section 3 Sub-section (ii), dated the 22"¢ April, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as 
the said notification) and issued under sub-section (l) of section 20A of the Railways (Amendment) Act, 2008 (] of 
2008) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declares its intention to acquire the land specified 
in the schedule annexed to the said notification for the purpose of execution, maintenance, management and operation 
of Special Railway Project, namely "Luni-Samdari-Bhildi Doubling Project of the District Jodhpur in the state 
of Rajasthan. 


And whereas, the substance of the said notification was published in daily newspapers namely “Rajasthan 
Patrika ” and “Dainik Bhaskar” dated 25th April, 2025 under sub section (4) of section 20A of the said Act; 


And whereas, , no objection was received within the stipulated time period to the competent authority. 


And, whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 20E of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


[भाग ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण ]7 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority, and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by sub-section (l) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declare that the land 
specified in the schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And, further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the official Gazette, the land specified in the schedule annexed hereto 
shall vest absolutely in the Central Government free from all encumbrances.

में, भारतीय सनदी लेखाकार संस्थान (आई.सी.ए.आई.) की परिषद्‌ के 37 मार्च 2025 को समाप्त वर्ष हेतु लेखापरीक्षित

वर्ष 2024-25 को ऐसी ऐतिहासिक अवधि के तौरपर याद किया जाएगा, जिसमें कई साहसिक विचार, परिवर्तनकारी 
कार्य और हमारे पेशे के भविष्य को आकार देने की प्रतिबद्धता देखने को मिली। चूँकि आई.सी.ए.आई. अपनी 75 वर्षों की 
SHEA का जश्न मना रहा है, हम एक निर्णायक मोड़ पर खड़े हैं, नए उद्देश्य व जुनून के साथ 'ETSAT@00' की ओर 
देख रहे हैं। आई.सी.ए.आई. की पहलों के केंद्र में क्षेत्र तकनीकी, अनुसंधान, संघ विकास, स्थिरता एवं पारदर्शिता का मूल 
निहित है, जो इस पेशे को उस दिशा में ले जा रहा है जिससे पेशे के अगले 25 वर्षों को आकार मिलेगा। विगत कुछ वर्षों 
में आई.सी.ए.आई. नियामक के तौरपर अपनी भूमिका से आगे बढ़कर वैश्विक स्तर पर सबसे बड़ी लेखा संस्था के रूप में 
उभरा है। आज, लेखा का पेशा परंपरा एवं परिवर्तन के दौर से गुज़र रहा है, जिसमें आई.सी.ए.आई. न केवल नियामक 
के तौरपर, बल्कि मूल्य सृजन हेतु भी परिवर्तन के उत्प्रेरक के रूप में अपनी भूमिका को बढ़ा रहा है। उद्देश्य की नई 
भावना के साथ, हमारा लक्ष्य न केवल अपनी कार्यप्रणाली का आधुनिकीकरण करना है, बल्कि वित्त के भविष्य की 
पुनर्कल्‍पना करना भी है। 


संस्थान के तौरपर, आई.सी.ए.आई. केवल पेशेवरों का ही नहीं, बल्कि समस्या-निवारकों, स्थिरता के समर्थकों एवं 
डिजिटल विचारकों का भी सृजन कर रहा है, जो ऐसी दुनिया की अगुवाई करने के लिए तैयार हैं, जिसमें दक्षता व

अर्थव्यवस्था (ग्रीन इकोनॉमी) में परिवर्तन को सक्षम बना रहा है, और यह सब ऐसे पेशे को आकार देने के ऐसे विश्वास से

8.4 लेखा परीक्षा समिति 


संस्थान की लेखा परीक्षा समिति की स्थापना अप्रैल 2007 में परिषद द्वारा एक गैर-स्थायी समिति के रूप में की गई थी, 
जिसका स्पष्ट रूप से तय अधिदेश था। 2009 से, इसकी अध्यक्षता एक विशेष सरकारी नामित व्यक्ति द्वारा की जाती 
रही है ताकि इसकी स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित की जा सके। इसकी स्वायत्तता को और बढ़ाने के लिए, कार्यकारी समिति एवं 
वित्त समिति के सदस्यों को केंद्रीय लेखा परीक्षा समिति में कार्य करने की अनुमति नहीं है। इसके अलावा, पाँच क्षेत्रीय 
लेखा परीक्षा समितियाँ--दक्षिणी, पश्चिमी, मध्य, उत्तरी और पूर्वी--समिति के कार्यों में सहयोग प्रदान करती हैं, जिससे 
क्षेत्रीय प्रतिनिधित्व और प्रभावी निगरानी सुनिश्चित होती है।

9.4 लेखा परीक्षा गुणवत्ता निदेशालय केंद्र (सीएक्यूडी) 


आई.सी.ए.आई. ने 2020 में लेखा परीक्षा गुणवत्ता निदेशालय केंद्र ("सीएक्यूडी") की स्थापना की, जो मुख्यतः ऑडिट 
फ़ंक्शन और ऑडिट गुणवत्ता के गुणात्मक पहलुओं का ध्यान रखता है। इस निदेशालय का एक विशेष प्रयोजन है, जो 
ऑडिट गुणवत्ता में निरंतर सुधार और भारतीय फर्म की वैश्विक स्थिति को बढ़ावा देना सुनिश्चित करता है। यह 
अनुसंधान हेतु अनुकूल परिवेश प्रदान करना और ऑडिट गुणवत्ता को बढ़ाने व बनाए रखने के मानदंड तय करने हेतु 
अधिक शोध-उन्मुख परियोजनाएं शुरू करने पर ध्यान देता Sl यह कानून प्रवर्तन में शामिल विभिन्न हितधारकों और 
नियामकों के बीच संबद्धता को बढ़ाकर ऑडिट गुणवत्ता पर अनुसंधान कार्यक्रमों का समर्थन करता है। लेखा परीक्षा 
गुणवत्ता निदेशालय केंद्र समकालीन क्षेत्रों पर अपेक्षित स्किल सेट को शामिल करने हेतु प्रतिभागियों के लिए विशेष 
अल्पकालिक अवधि के पाठ्यक्रमों के माध्यम से पेशेवर लेखाकारों और लेखा परीक्षकों के लिए समकालीन शिक्षा और 
प्रशिक्षण में निरंतर निवेश का लक्ष्य रखता है।

परिषद इस पेशे से जुड़े उन सभी सदस्यों की आभारी है जिन्होंने इसकी समितियों में सहयोजित सदस्यों के रूप में कार्य

2024-25 के दौरान परिषद की शैक्षिक, तकनीकी और अन्य विकासात्मक गतिविधियों के संचालन और इसकी

हेतु उनकी सराहना करती है। 


परिषद आईसीएआई द्वारा की गई अनेक पहलों तथा इन पहलों के अनुसरण में उनके द्वारा पहले से उठाए जा रहे/उठाए

हमने भारतीय Aes अकाउंटेंटस संस्थान (“संस्थान”) के संलग्न वित्तीय विवरणों, जिसमें 34 मार्च, 2025 को यथा 
विद्यमान तुलनपत्र और उस तारीख को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए संलग्न आय और व्यय लेखा तथा नकद प्रवाह विवरण 
और वित्तीय विवरणों संबंधी टिप्पणों की संपरीक्षा की है, जिसके अंतर्गत महत्वपूर्ण लेखांकन नीतियों का संक्षिप्त विवरण 
और अन्य स्पष्टीकारक जानकारी भी है (जिसे इसमें इसके पश्चात्‌ “वित्तीय विवरण” कहा गया है), जिसमें संस्थान के 
विकेन्द्रीकृत कार्यालयों, विदेशी कार्यालयों, उत्कृष्टता केंद्रों प्रादेशिक परिषदों और उनकी शाखाओं के शाखा संपरीक्षकों 
द्वारा संपरीक्षित विवरणियों/वित्तीय विवरणों को भी सम्मिलित किया गया है। 


हमारी राय में और हमारी सर्वोत्तम पूर्वोक्त वित्तीय विवरण चार्टर्ड अकाउंटेंट्स अधिनियम, 7949 (आज की तारीख तक 
यथा संशोधित) द्वारा अपेक्षित रीति में अपेक्षित जानकारी प्रदान करता है और वे भारत में साधारण रूप से स्वीकृत 
लेखांकन सिद्धांतों के अनुसार तारीख 3 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए संस्थान की वित्तीय स्थिति और उसके 
अधिशेष तथा नकद प्रवाह के संबंध में एक सत्य और उचित मत प्रदान करते हैं |

रिपोर्ट में, जहां तक वह रकम और प्रकटन से संबंधित है, पूर्णतया असंपरीक्षित वित्तीय विवरणों/जानकारी पर आधारित 
हैं। हमें दी गई जानकारी और दिए गए स्पष्टीकरणों के अनुसार, ये वित्तीय विवरण/जानकारी संस्थान के लिए सारवान नहीं हैं । 
हमारी राय को उपरोक्त मामलों के संबंध में उपांतरित नहीं किया गया है। 

अन्य विनियामक अपेक्षाओं पर रिपोर्ट 

हम यह और रिपोर्ट करते हैं कि: 


क) हमने ऐसी सभी जानकारी और स्पष्टीकरण प्राप्त किए हैं जो हमारे सर्वोत्तम ज्ञान और विश्वास के अनुसार 
हमारी संपरीक्षा के प्रयोजन के लिए आवश्यक थे ; 


ख) हमारी राय में, जहां तक लेखा बहियों की हमारी परीक्षा से प्रतीत होता है, संस्थान द्वारा समुचित लेखा 
बहियां रखी गई हैं और हमारी संपरीक्षा के प्रयोजन के लिए शाखाओं, जहां हमने दौरा नहीं किया है, से 
समुचित और पर्याप्त विवरणियां प्राप्त हुई हैं ; 

ग) संस्थान की शाखाओं के लेखाओं, जिनकी संपरीक्षा शाखा संपरीक्षकों द्वारा की गई है, संबंधी रिपोर्टों को हमें 
अग्रेषित किया गया है और हमने इस रिपोर्ट को तैयार करते समय उनके संबंध में उपयुक्त रूप से कार्यवाही की है ; 


घ) इस रिपोर्ट से संबंधित संस्थान का तुलन पत्र, आय और व्यय लेखा और नकद प्रवाह विवरण, लेखा बहियों के 
अनुरूप है और वे ऐसी शाखाओं से प्राप्त विवरणियों के भी अनुरूप है, जिनका हमने दौरा नहीं किया है।

catalyst championing change for value creation. With a renewed sense of purpose, we are not just to modernize

As an institution, ICAI is building more than professionals, cultivating problem-solvers, sustainability champions, 
and digital thinkers who are ready to lead in a world that demands agility and accountability. The Institute is 
strengthening governance, evolving accounting frameworks, and actively enabling the transition to a green

and drives the nation forward with purpose and pride. With India now standing tall as the world’s fourth-largest 
economy and steadily progressing toward the ambitious goal of becoming a $30 trillion powerhouse, the nation is 
redefining global leadership. In this transformative era, ICAI remains deeply committed to being a trusted partner 
in nation building, firmly rooted in its role as a guardian of public interest and a catalyst for sustainable progress. 


Renowned globally for its ethics, technical excellence, and rigorous education, ICAI continues to shape 
professionals who are not only financially adept but also socially responsible. Chartered Accountants have long 
been vital contributors to India’s economic story as advisors, enablers, and changemakers across industries and 
communities. As look ahead, ICAI stands ready to lead with integrity, foster innovation, and nurture talent that can 
thrive in a dynamic, technology-driven world. With innovative ideas and commitment to excellence, the Institute is 
shaping the narrative of India’s global rise. Over the past 75 years, ICAI has not only upheld the trust of the nation 
but also helped shape its financial narrative by building a legacy of credibility, excellence, and national service. As 
India emerges as the fourth-largest economy in the world and sets its sights on becoming a $30 trillion economic 
force, the role of the accounting profession is more crucial than ever. 


Today, the Institute stands at a powerful intersection of legacy and change. With a deep commitment to ethical

75 Years of Trust- Celebrating the Excellence, Independence and Integrity of the CA Profession 


ICAI celebrated Ist July 2024 as 75 years of trust, honouring Chartered Accountants hard work and contributions 
to national development. The event was marked with great enthusiasm and splendor, showcasing the achievements 
of Chartered Accountants and future plans in the Kartavya Kaal to realize the vision of Viksit Bharat. The grand 
event, held in the largest hall of Bharat Mandapam, was attended by numerous dignitaries and all CAs. Among 
them were Minister of Road Transport and Highways of India; Attorney General of India; Secretary of the Ministry 
of Electronics and Information Technology; Secretary of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, President of the 
Institute of Chartered Accountants of Bangladesh; Confederation of Asian and Pacific Accountants (CAPA) 
President; Shri Heshana Kuruppu President of South Asian Federation of Accountants (SAFA). 


ICAI unites for a nationwide ‘CA Run for Viksit Bharat’ 


The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), the world's largest accountancy body, commemorated its 75 
years of service to the nation with the grand 'CA Run for Viksit Bharat' on 30" June, 2024. The event underscored 
ICAI’s commitment to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of transforming India into a developed nation by 
2047. More than 0000 Participants participated, including members and students from across the globe, began the 
run at 6:00 AM from 5 Regional Councils, !76 Branches, and various Chapters. In New Delhi, the run commenced 
from ICAI Headquarters and concluded at Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium. The event was graced by the 
presence of Shri Harsh Malhotra, Hon’ble Minister of State of Corporate Affairs, who praised ICAI’s contributions 
to the nation's financial standards. ICAI leadership emphasized the profession's role in economic reforms and good 
governance and highlighted the collective dedication of the CA fraternity towards a prosperous India. 


World Forum of Accountants -2025 


The World Forum of Accountants (WOFA) 2025, a prestigious global convergence of accounting professionals and 
thought leaders, was organized by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) and inaugurated by 
Hon’ble Defence Minister of India. Held from January 3] to February 2, 2025, at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, the 
event brought together over 6,500 delegates from 46 countries — marking one of the largest and most significant 
gatherings of the global accounting fraternity. Centered on the theme "Accountability Meets Innovation (Al): For a 
Sustainable Planet," WOFA 2025 served as a dynamic platform for exchanging insights on emerging global trends, 
sustainable practices, and the transformative role of technology in the accounting profession. More than just a 
conference, WOFA became a moment of pride and powerful assertion of India’s growing stature in the global 
financial ecosystem. With this landmark event, ICAI showcased India’s capabilities as a rising global hub for 
accounting and auditing services. The Forum reflected India’s vision of becoming a knowledge leader in assurance, 
transparency, and financial stewardship,aligned with the broader national aspiration of positioning India as a 
trusted voice and destination in the global economy. 


Training of Indian Corporate Law Services (ICLS) Officials 


Being a premier educational body the ICAI continuously endeavours to support the capacity and competency 
development of government officials for building their understanding on various emerging aspects of financial 
reporting and laws as well as the evolving best practices. In this direction, the institute has conducted training for 
ICLS officials 2022 batch at ICAI Head Quarters, New Delhi on 20th April, 2024. With these initiatives the 
institute aspires to strengthen the process of developing effective and efficient policy for better governance. 


ICAI adopts Tech for enhancing Financial Literacy — Finfluencer Meet 


Surveys reveal that only 27 per cent of India's population is financially literate. Additionally, only 6.7 per cent of 
Indian students have a basic understanding of finance and money management. As the world's largest accounting 
body, ICAI as its social responsibility is educating and empowering the citizens of the country and create a 
sustainable financial ecosystem for the nation to emerge as a self-reliant nation. Taking forward the Government of 
India’s mission of ‘VitiyaSaksharta’ (Financial Literacy) to the next level and promoting understanding of tax laws, 
accounting, and diverse facets of the financial system. The institute has organized a Finfluencers meet in New 
Delhi on 50 April, 2024 wherein 4] prominent social media influencers came forward to collaborate and on 
educating masses on financial knowledge. 


Academia Meet with Universities & Institutions 


With a vision to make India Vishwaguru, the ICAI organised the Academia Meet with Universities and Institutions 
held on May 7, 2024, in New Delhi. The event served as a vital platform for meaningful dialogue between ICAI 
and academia, bringing together scholars, researchers, and senior faculty from over 35 leading universities and 
institutions across the country. The discussions focused on fostering a collaborative ecosystem for academic 
research, aligning curriculum with evolving industry needs, and exploring joint initiatives to promote innovation, 
ethics, and excellence in commerce and accountancy education. This engagement reflects ICAI’s firm commitment 
to strengthening academic partnerships, encouraging applied research, and shaping future-ready professionals 
through an enriched and forward-looking education framework.

ICAI enters into MoU with CBSE 


The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) through its Committee on Career Counselling signed a MoU 
with the Department of Skill Education, Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) on 2["/ November 2024, at 
Bhubaneswar, Odisha, to promote commerce-based skill courses for students across the country. The partnership

designed to align with industry requirements. 


Supporting Government Accounting Reforms - Strengthening Financial Management in Indian Railways 


The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), through its Accounting Research Foundation (ICAI ARF), 
has been at the forefront of driving financial reforms in Indian Railways, significantly enhancing its financial 
management framework. Since 20l4, ICAI ARF has served as the technical partner in Indian Railways' ambitious 
Accounting Reforms initiative, marking a major shift towards transparency, accountability, and efficiency. As a 
part of this collaboration, ICAI ARF has successfully developed and submitted accrual-based financial statements 
for Indian Railways for six consecutive years (20!7—l8 to 2022-23). This transition from cash-based to accrual- 
based accounting has enabled Indian Railways to gain deeper insights into asset and liability management, better 
evaluate performance, and improve financial decision-making. 


ICAI - Moving Towards Sustainable Planet 


The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) is leading efforts towards a sustainable future by 
introducing initiatives like SSAE 3000 and SAE 340 for sustainability and greenhouse gas assurance, and the 
Sustainability Reporting Maturity Model. ICAI promotes accountability through its Sustainability Reporting 
Awards and the Institute of Social Auditors of India, which issues thematic Social Audit Standards. The Green 
Mahotsav campaign pledges to plant 00,000 trees, symbolizing environmental commitment. This initiative also 
resonated with national leadership’s campaign ‘Ek Ped Ma Ke Naam’, which encourages every citizen to plant a 
tree in the name of their mother. ICAI also developed a Carbon Emission Calculator covering Scope |, 2, and 3 
emissions to help individuals and organizations measure and reduce their carbon footprint. Additionally, ICAI 
supports the LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) initiative, encouraging mindful consumption and responsible living 
among its vast member and student network. Through these efforts, ICAI aims to inspire sustainable practices and 
lead impactful environmental change. 


ICAI MSME & Startup Yatra in Asia and India Book of Records 


The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) is dedicated to empowering MSMEs, women, and youth 
through initiatives like Startup Sphere, Startup Manthan and MSME and Startup Yatra, fostering entrepreneurship 
and job creation. Recognized in the Asia and India Book of Records for awareness drives in over l00 cities within 
00 days, ICAI promotes a self-reliant economy through key events such as the MSME & Startup Conclave on 26% 
& 27 June, 2025 and the nationwide MSME Mahotsav on 27" June, 2025. The conclave gathered over 3,000 
stakeholders to support innovation and capacity building, while the Mahotsav offered free Udyam registration, 
consultations, and grievance redressal for MSMEs. Additionally, ICAI signed an MoU with the National Small 
Industries Corporation (NSIC) on June 27, 2025, to enhance MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship 
development, and integrated support services including marketing, technology, finance, and global outreach. These 
initiatives highlight ICAI’s pivotal role in advancing India’s MSME and startup ecosystem. 


ICAI Reforms Exam Structure - More Chances, More Success 


To align with global best practices and offer students more opportunities, the 26" Council of ICAI has decided to 
conduct the CA Final exam three times a year instead of twice. Last year, ICAI made a similar change for the 
Intermediate and Foundation exams, and now all three levels will have equal exam attempts in January, May, and 
September. Additionally, the Post Qualification Course in Information Systems Audit will also shift from biannual 
to thrice-yearly assessments in February, June, and October. These changes aim to enhance flexibility, 
accessibility, and professional growth for students and members. These historic decisions will ensure that both 
students and professionals have abundant opportunities to succeed and excel in their careers. 


ICAI Sets New Benchmarks in Skill Enrichment and Entrepreneurship Development 


ICAI has been recognized by the India Book of Records and Asia Book of Records for two major achievements i.e 
conducting 97 entrepreneurship skill programs in a single day and 79 skill enrichment programs within I5 days. 
These milestones highlight ICAI’s strong commitment to fostering entrepreneurship, continuous learning, and 
building a future-ready workforce in the accounting and finance sectors.

Integrating Technology: Transforming the Profession 


In 2024—25, ICAI launched the Committee on Artificial Intelligence to drive AI adoption in education, operations, 
and member services. Key initiatives included the AICA Certificate Course ((50+ batches, 5,000+ members), 9 
CA GPT modules benefiting |.2 lakh users, and specialized GPTs for regulatory tasks. ICAI also advanced digital 
transformation through e-Office, centralized document management, real-time dashboards, and the ‘ICAI 
Diaspora’ mobile app for overseas members. Collaborating with MeitY on DigiLocker, ICAI continues to 
modernize and lead the profession in the digital age. It has introduced the Al-powered ‘ICAI AI Agent’ digital 
workspace, with plans to extend it to members and students. Additionally, ICAI developed the world’s first 
Forensic Accounting and Investigating Standards to enhance digital financial reporting and is working towards 
their global adoption, positioning itself at the forefront of AI integration in accounting.

members for future challenges, ICAI introduced various certificate courses in fund management, capital market 
compliance, skill enrichment, mediation, and an online German language course. Collaborations with institutions

This state-of-the-art center aims to enhance professional excellence through advanced learning, research, and skill

5. Disciplinary Directorate 


The Disciplinary Directorate, the regulatory arm of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), has been 
established to investigate cases of Professional and/or Other Misconduct alleged against its members. These cases 
may be received through a Formal Complaint in Form I or via the Information route, as provided under the 
Chartered Accountants Act, 949 read with The Chartered Accountants (Procedure of Investigations of 
Professional and Other Misconduct and Conduct of Cases) Rules, 2007. Under the disciplinary framework, the 
Disciplinary Directorate has a statutory obligation to examine all alleged lapses or irregularities committed by 
members across India. This mechanism not only helps maintain public confidence and trust in the profession but 
also sets a benchmark for acceptable professional conduct. While the vast majority of Chartered Accountants 
continue to offer dedicated and ethical services to society through their expertise, the disciplinary process ensures 
that the few who stray intentionally or inadvertently are duly corrected. 


Following the 2006 amendments to the Chartered Accountants Act, 949, ICAI's disciplinary framework was 
significantly strengthened to expedite the resolution of disciplinary cases. Consequently, the disciplinary 
mechanism currently operates through two quasi-judicial bodies established under the Chartered Accountants 
(Amendment) Act, 2006: 


e ~— Board of Discipline (BoD) under Section 2lA 
e = Disciplinary Committee (DC) under Section 2!B 


This structure ensures transparency, enhances stakeholder confidence, and guarantees fair and equitable justice for 
members facing allegations. To further enhance accountability and expedite justice, additional amendments were 
made to the Chartered Accountants Act, /949 in the year 2022. However, the date from which these revised 
disciplinary provisions will come into effect is yet to be notified. During the Council year 2024-25, for efficient 
case management and swift resolution, five Benches of the Disciplinary Committee—Bench I, II, IH, IV, and V 
(handling MNAF cases)—and one Bench of the Board of Discipline were constituted. These benches worked 
actively on cases under enquiry, including reviewing Prima Facie Opinions formed by the Director (Discipline). 
Additionally, the Disciplinary Committee under Section 2!D, chaired by the ICAI President, was constituted to 
address residual legacy cases that are/may be referred back under the old disciplinary mechanism. 


(I) Key Initiatives and Achievements 


e E-Hearings: The Directorate successfully conducted e-hearings with effective participation from 
members of the BoD and DC as well as parties. These hearings proved highly beneficial by saving time and 
cost and enabling broader participation by the parties without the burden of travel. The increased disposal 
rate of cases is a testament to their effectiveness. 


e Revamped Web Portal: Recognizing the need for modernization, the existing web portal of the 
Disciplinary Directorate i.e https://disc.icai.org has been comprehensively revamped. The revamped portal 
now serves as a one-stop destination for all information related to the Disciplinary mechanism. It has been 
thoughtfully redesigned to highlight key updates such as recent meetings and Orders/Findings passed by the 
Board of Discipline (BOD) and the Disciplinary Committee (DC) directly on the homepage. The new 
structure ensures that stakeholders can access relevant information more efficiently. It now aligns with the 
ICAI’s official colour theme for a consistent visual identity. 


e Capacity Building: To enhance operational efficiency and keep pace with developments in laws and 
regulations, regular training sessions are conducted for the Directorate’s officials and staff. These sessions 
cover crucial topics such as Corporate Laws, CARO, and Ind AS etc., ensuring that the team remains 
efficient, competent and updated. 


e = Training on Artificial Intelligence: Embracing the potential of emerging technologies, a specialised 
three-day training programme on Artificial Intelligence was organized in May 2025 with the help of the 'AI 
in ICAI Committee’. Tailored to the specific needs of the Disciplinary Directorate, this programme aimed at 
equipping Directorate’s Officers with the knowledge and skills necessary to harness AI tools effectively in

The Accounting Standards Board (ASB), established by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) in

financial reporting in India. Its primary objectives are to harmonize accounting practices across the country and to 
align Indian standards with the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) issued by the International 
Accounting Standards Board (IASB). Over time, the ASB has actively revised existing standards and developed

6.2 Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (AASB) 


Audit plays a critical role in protecting public interest by enhancing accountability and fostering trust in financial 
reporting, thereby supporting economic growth. Increasing business complexity and expanding global operations 
have heightened stakeholder expectations of the auditing profession. In response, the ICAI’s Auditing and 
Assurance Standards Board (AASB) develops high-quality Standards on Auditing, Review, Assurance, Quality 
Control, and Related Services, which set best practices and serve as benchmarks for auditor performance.The 
Board also issues Guidance Notes on general and industry-specific auditing issues to provide practical support to 
auditors. These are released under the ICAI Council’s authority, except for auditing standards related to companies 
and Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs), where the Central Government prescribes standards based on ICAI’s

6.3 Expert Advisory Committee (EAC) 


In the current prevailing economic environment, marked by complex transactions and a continually evolving 
financial reporting framework, accounting professionals are increasingly confronted with challenging situation that 
require careful interpretation and application of such framework including accounting and auditing principles to 
novel transactions. This gives rise to the need for credible and well-researched solutions in such situations to 
uphold the integrity and reliability of financial reporting. The extensively researched and deliberated opinions 
issued by the Expert Advisory Committee play a pivotal role in supporting the accounting professionals and 
preparers of financial statements by offering the guidance on the complex accounting situations/transactions. Since 
its inception, the Committee has been continuously providing opinions on the matters referred to it by the members 
of the Institute across all industries as well as by the government and regulatory bodies. 


(0) Expert Opinions 


The Committee answers queries received from the members of the ICAI in accordance with Advisory Service 
Rules. As per Rules, the Committee answers queries relating to accounting and/or auditing principles and does not 
answer queries which involve only legal interpretation of various enactments. It also does not answer queries which 
involve professional misconduct or on a matter pending before the Disciplinary Committee of the Institute, any 
court of law, the Income-tax authorities or any other appropriate department of the Government. These Rules are 
available on the website of the ICAI, at its link, https://www.icai.org/post/495 or can be obtained from the 
Institute’s Head Office at New Delhi. The opinions issued by the Expert Advisory Committee are based on the 
specific facts and circumstances provided by the querist, taking into account the relevant laws, statutes, and 
applicable accounting and auditing principles. Each opinion clearly states the date of its finalisation and should be 
read considering the developments and/or amendments to laws or standards, that may have occurred after that date.

6.4 Financial Reporting Review Board (FRRB)

reporting and auditing practices prevailing in India. It was constituted by ICAI as a proactive initiative to improve

practical insights into procedural intricacies, fostering greater expertise and efficiency in insolvency resolution 
practices. 


A Study on the Efficacy of IBC, 206 in meeting deadlines and maximizing value during the Corporate

Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP), their impact on asset realization values, and the prevalence of defunct 
companies under CIRP. By examining these factors and offering actionable recommendations, the study aims 
to provide as a guide towards enhancing the efficiency and efficacy of insolvency proceedings, fostering a 
more robust resolution framework in India.

significant part of a company's value. This publication offers practical insights, case studies, and detailed 
guidance on valuation practices in accordance with ICAI Valuation Standards 208. It supports consistent and 
uniform practices across India and contributes to enhancing the efficiency and expertise of valuers, ultimately 
fostering transparency and stability in financial markets.

real estate projects, revising fees for creditor representatives, and ensuring timely committee meetings.

6.5 Ethical Standards Board (ESB) 


The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India has constituted the Ethical Standards Board as the designated 
standard-setting authority for ethical governance within the profession. The Board is vested with the mandate to 
develop and implement ethical standards and other authoritative pronouncements applicable to Chartered 
Accountants. In fulfilling its mandate, the Board endeavours to evolve a dynamic and contemporary Code of Ethics 
and ethical framework for members, while upholding the time-honoured principles of excellence, independence, 
and integrity, thereby safeguarding the dignity and interests of the members. The objective of the Ethical Standards 
Board is to formulate and promulgate ethical standards for Chartered Accountants that align with internationally 
recognized best practices, subject to compliance with applicable domestic laws. Through this alignment, the Board 
aims to enhance the quality, consistency, and reliability of services rendered by Chartered Accountants, thereby 
reinforcing public confidence and trust in the profession. 


Since its inception, the Board has diligently engaged in establishing and maintaining standards that regulate the 
professional conduct and qualification of ICAI members. In addition to its core responsibilities, the Board actively

6.6 Digital Accounting and Assurance Board (DAAB) 


The Digital Accounting and Assurance Board (DAAB) traces its roots to the year 2000, when ICAI established the 
Committee on Information Technology (CIT) to spearhead the profession’s IT initiatives. In its first decade, CIT 
focused on raising IT awareness, introducing the Information Systems Audit (ISA) course, and building basic 
technology infrastructure for members. In 2009, the committee broadened the scope by including forensic 
accounting, XBRL implementation, e-learning, and greater technology integration into audit practices. Recognizing 
the accelerating digital transformation in finance, ICAI reconstituted this committee as the Digital Accounting and 
Assurance Board (DAAB) in 209, with an expanded mandate covering digital competencies, forensic standards, 
blockchain, AI, and global partnerships. This evolution over two decades laid the groundwork for a proactive body 
attuned to the emerging challenges and opportunities of the digital era. 


(I) Key Milestones and Initiatives 


e DISA Launches and Upgrades: The journey began with the launch of the Post-Qualification course on 
Information Systems Audit (ISA) in 2000, which provided Chartered Accountants specialized training in IT 
auditing. This program later, undergone multiple syllabus revisions (DISA .0, 2.0, 3.0) to keep pace with 
technological advances. Over the years, DISA gained formal recognition from regulators notably the 
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and market authorities enabling DISA-qualified members to conduct bank 
system audits as experts. Today, DAAB is in the process of rolling out DISA 4.0, a comprehensive upgrade 
that will incorporate cybersecurity frameworks, data privacy (DPDP Act) compliance, regulatory 
technology (RegTech), and other emerging areas into the curriculum. 


e Forensic Accounting and Fraud Detection (FAFD) Course: Recognizing the growing need for forensic 
expertise, ICAI launched the Certificate Course on Forensic Accounting and Fraud Detection (FAFD) in 
2009, equipping members with investigative skills supported by hands-on training through forensic labs, 
including one established in Noida in 207. As the field evolved, DAAB continually upgraded the course— 
most notably aligning it in 2023 with ICAI’s world-first Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards 
(FAIS), now mandatory for forensic assignments. In 2024, DAAB initiated the course's transition into a full- 
fledged Diploma in Forensic Investigation (DFI), which received initial approval from the Ministry of 
Corporate Affairs and is set for public exposure before final clearance—marking a major step in advancing 
formal forensic education. 


e __ Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards (FAIS): A landmark achievement of the DAAB era 
has been the development of Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards (FAIS) — a comprehensive 
framework to guide practitioners in forensic accounting engagements. Released in series (totalling 20 
individual standards and 3 overarching documents) and refined through expert input, the FAIS were 
officially issued with mandatory implementation from 2023 onwards. These standards cover the entire 
gamut of forensic accounting, from evidence collection and analysis to reporting, and serve as a definitive 
benchmark for quality and consistency in forensic services undertaken by chartered accountants. 


e _ Digital Competency Maturity Model (DCMM): To help the profession assess and improve its adoption 
of technology, the Board developed the Digital Competency Maturity Model (DCMM) Version | and in 
209, DCMM 2.0, its implementation guide and a tool was released which provides a structured model with 
defined levels and an implementation guide for firms to evaluate their digital capabilities. Further, it was 
made part of Peer review also. By benchmarking areas such as IT infrastructure, software tools, process 
automation, and digital skills, DCMM has enabled audit firms (especially small and medium practices) to 
identify gaps and roadmaps for digital transformation. The model’s relevance has extended beyond India — it 
has been showcased in international forums and adapted by global accounting groups as a tool for enhancing 
digital practices in the accounting profession. 


e International Outreach : From its early years, DAAB has extended its impact internationally. In the mid- 
2000s, ICAI’s IT Committee began delivering ISA courses in Sri Lanka and Nepal, supported by MoUs 
with ICASL and ICAN. These collaborations later expanded to include forensic accounting training. By 
2025, ICASL expressed interest in adopting ICAI’s forensic standards, reflecting their global relevance. 
DAAB has also conducted virtual DISA classes for professionals in both countries and hosted international 
participants in its programs. A key example was the customized FAFD training for Bank of Bhutan auditors 
in October 2024. These efforts have strengthened ICAI’s global standing in digital accounting and 
assurance.
